findings.summary: An additive process is a cadlag stochastic process with independent increments and continuity in probability, generalizing Lévy processes by relaxing the stationary increments requirement. It can model complex phenomena with time-dependent drift or volatility. Key mechanisms include independent increments, continuity in probability, and the Lévy–Khintchine representation defining the process via a generating triplet of drift, covariance, and Lévy measure. Subclasses such as additive subordinators, Sato processes, and additive normal tempered stable processes extend the framework for specific applications. Simulation leverages increment independence for computational efficiency, using techniques like jump truncation, Gaussian approximation, and characteristic function inversion with Fast Fourier transform.

mechanisms.title: Independent Increments
mechanisms.explanation: The process has independent increments if for any 0 ≤ p < r ≤ s < t, the increment X_t - X_s is independent of X_r - X_p. This property allows separate simulation of increments and enables parallelization.

mechanisms.title: Lévy–Khintchine Representation
mechanisms.explanation: An additive process at time t has an infinitely divisible distribution characterized by a generating triplet (γ_t, A_t, ν_t): γ_t is a drift vector, A_t is a covariance matrix, and ν_t is a Lévy measure satisfying ν_t({0}) = 0 and ∫(1 ∧ x²)ν_t(dx) < ∞. The characteristic function is explicitly given by the Lévy–Khintchine formula.
